claims.evidence: INS-1E is a rat insulinoma line (Cellosaurus CVCL_0351, NCBITaxon 10116). PRIDE organisms list both rat and mouse; the PD search database contains MOUSE_2013-06-30.fasta plus uniprot-rat.fasta, so the mouse entry is treated as a search database artefact, not a sample organism.

claims.evidence: Cellosaurus record (sex Male, breed NEDH, disease Rat insulinoma); PRIDE title/description name INS-1E cells in the sample processing protocol.

claims.location: comment[label] and characteristics[sampling time]/[treatment]/factor value[sampling time]
claims.value: SILAC light=0 min, SILAC medium=2 min, SILAC heavy=5 min after 17 mM glucose
claims.evidence: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol: '0 minute (light), 2 minutes (medium), 5 minutes (heavy)'; PD quantification method 'SILAC 3plex (Arg6, Lys4 | Arg10, Lys8)'. Applied identically to all three replicates; replicate-specific label swaps could not be excluded (paper full text unavailable).

claims.value: FUS* files: Orbitrap Fusion (MS:1002416); QHF_* files: Q Exactive HF (MS:1002523)
claims.evidence: All 52 raw headers decoded: 28 FUS files contain 'Orbitrap Fusion', 24 QHF files contain 'Q Exactive HF'. PRIDE lists only 'Q Exactive', which is incomplete/wrong.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; Oxidation M, protein N-term Acetyl, SILAC Lys/Arg labels variable
claims.evidence: Sequest HT node: StaticModification1 Carbamidomethyl (UNIMOD 4), DynamicModification1-5 Oxidation(35), Label:13C(2)15N(2) K (1787), Label:13C(6)15N(2) K (259), Label:13C(6) R (188), Label:13C(6)15N(4) R (267), DynamicModificationNProtein Acetyl (1).
Sequest HT Enzyme: Trypsin, KR, inhibitor P, MaxMissedCleavages 2. PRIDE prose does not name the enzyme.
Sequest HT PeptideTolerance 10 ppm, FragmentTolerance 0.5 Da. PRIDE prose states 2 ppm / 0.05 Da (2 ppm is the Event Detector mass precision); the deposited search wins.
PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol: peptide separation by hydrophilic interaction chromatography.

INFERRED, NOT a verified HILIC fraction rank: a run-order index (1..18 rep1/rep2, 1..16 rep3). Files are numbered in the msf WorkflowInputFiles order: within a replicate FUS files first, then QHF files, each in numeric order. The deposit states no fraction rank. Rep2: QHF_003943 (91 KB) and QHF_003943_CORRUPTED are listed in the msf but not deposited, so QHF_003944 is indexed directly after QHF_003942 (17 of 18 deposited QHF/FUS files in sequence); if 003943 held a real fraction, indices after it would shift by one. Consumers should treat the value only as a unique per-file index within a replicate.
PRIDE: stimulated with 17 mM glucose; the concentration is recorded here and in the report because the NCIT/EFO-backed column takes only a term.

limitations: Full text of the paper was not accessible; culture medium, passage number, storage temperature, dissociation method, reduction/alkylation reagents and developmental stage are not available.
Fraction identifiers are a run-order index, not a verified HILIC fraction rank.
SILAC channel to time-point mapping comes from PRIDE prose and is assumed identical across replicates.
FUS05832_TK.raw is 45 KB and QHF_003943 is absent from PRIDE; the 45 KB file is annotated as deposited but probably holds no usable spectra.
PRIDE's instrument field (Q Exactive) disagrees with the raw headers; the raw headers were used.
Fraction identifier is a run-order index (see claim); this is a documented limitation, not verified fractionation order.
Glucose concentration (17 mM) is not encoded in the SDRF cell, only in this manifest and the report.

The PD Precursor Ions Quantifier defines medium as Lys4 (Label:2H(4), UNIMOD:481)+Arg6 and heavy as Lys8+Arg10, whereas the Sequest search lists Label:13C(2)15N(2) K (UNIMOD:1787); the SDRF follows the Sequest search verbatim, so UNIMOD:481 is absent.
